blocks.title: The modern periodic law
blocks.text: The physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom. The law is the cornerstone of the periodic table: elements with similar properties appear at certain intervals. When the elements are arranged by increasing atomic number, sodium, potassium and cesium show many physical and chemical characteristics similar to lithium, because they all fall in the same group. But because the number of protons in the nucleus rises gradually and new electron shells are added, the physical and chemical properties of elements vary systematically within a group and within a period.
